problem.text: Ordinary MLP previously fixed its down projection's output width to hidden_size, preventing independently sized outputs.

reasoning.text: The new optional out_size controls only the down projection. None preserves hidden_size; the up projection, activation and forward sequence remain unchanged.

impact.text: The whole-tree MLP search found one ordinary MLP construction site, in Gemma3 vision. It uses keyword arguments and omits out_size, preserving its existing dimensions. GatedMLP is unchanged.
Inserting out_size before key_up changes positional binding for external callers that supplied optional arguments positionally; the inspected in-tree caller does not do so.

source_notes.text: Read the initial modules entry and the ordinary-MLP alignment and activation entries. They establish the original projection pipeline, configurable alignment and subsequent activation selection.

The earlier ignored-activation observation is no longer present: the parent selects SiLU or GELU. Its unsupported-activation observation persists because this patch changes neither selection nor forward dispatch.

Issue #38, “Error converting nvidia/Llama-3_1-Nemotron-Ultra-253B-v1,” concerns sliced GatedMLP loading. Issues #34, “torch._C._LinAlgError on last layer of quant,” and #42, “converting to 3.0 bpw causes error; block state has 0 inf values and 34 NaN values,” concern quantization failures. Their relationship here is inferred only from shared mlp.py or linear.py paths; none establishes a motivation or fix for ordinary MLP output sizing.

limitations: No model, PyTorch operation, weight loader or GPU kernel was executed. The scalar check validates dimension arithmetic only, not backend support for arbitrary widths.
Literal whole-tree searches do not establish compatibility for dynamic or external callers.

claims.text: MLP now constructs hidden_size → intermediate_size → out_size projections, falling back to hidden_size when out_size is None. Forward still applies up, the selected activation, down, and output-dtype conversion; it introduces no residual projection or output cropping.

out_size remains subject to Linear's alignment: dimensions round upward to multiples of pad_to, whose default 128 is an alignment quantum, not a token threshold. pad_to=1 preserves exact widths. Both MLP projections retain the input-padding assertion, so default alignment still requires aligned hidden and intermediate dimensions.

A standard-library transcription with hidden=128 and intermediate=256 produced down dimensions (256,128) for the default output, (256,256) for out_size=130 with alignment 128, and (256,130) with alignment 1. All three satisfied the inspected input-alignment conditions.

TransformerBlock and ParallelDecoderBlock still add MLP results directly to their residual tensors; neither adapts the residual width. Their interfaces therefore do not generally accommodate independently sized outputs. Gemma3's existing keyword-based MLP construction retains the default equal width, while its separate multimodal Linear projection remains unchanged.

findings.description: Unsupported activation strings still leave ordinary MLP's activation callable unset.
findings.trigger: An external caller constructs an otherwise valid MLP with activation_fn="relu" and calls forward after loading its projections.
findings.expected_behavior: Reject the unsupported selection explicitly or provide a defined activation.
findings.actual_behavior: Neither match arm assigns activation_fn_call, so forward accesses a missing attribute after the up projection. The only identified in-tree constructor uses supported GELU; this trigger is limited to the exposed API.

verification.description: Compared parent activation dispatch with the complete task diff and inspected the constructor caller and transformer consumers.
verification.limits: No MLP execution or external caller inspection.

annotation.summary: Adds optional ordinary-MLP output sizing while preserving default dimensions and existing alignment requirements; residual consumers remain unchanged.
